The objective is to provide an aluminum plate that exhibits favorable adhesiveness and coating properties for active materials while maintaining a high level of mechanical strength. Such an aluminum plate is particularly suitable for applications in which an active material must be firmly supported on the plate surface and uniformly applied, without significantly reducing the durability or structural integrity of the plate.

The aluminum plate includes a plurality of through holes formed therein. These through holes have an average opening diameter within a range of 0.1 μm to 100 μm. By controlling the average opening diameter within this range, it is possible to improve the ability of the active material to adhere to the plate and to enhance coating uniformity, while avoiding excessive weakening of the aluminum plate.

The plurality of through holes also has an average opening ratio of 2% to 40%. The opening ratio refers to the proportion of the plate surface occupied by the openings of the through holes. When the average opening ratio is within this range, the plate can provide sufficient surface structure for anchoring or retaining the active material, while still preserving adequate strength and handling properties.

In addition, the distribution of the through-hole opening diameters is controlled. Specifically, no more than 40% of the through holes have an opening diameter of 5 μm or less, and no more than 40% of the through holes have an opening diameter of 40 μm or more. Limiting the proportion of very small and very large through holes helps ensure a balanced pore structure. This contributes to stable coating performance, improved adhesion of the active material, and prevention of excessive strength reduction caused by overly large openings.

Furthermore, at least 50% of the through holes have a shape ratio S1/S0 within a range of 0.1 to 1. In this relationship, S1 represents the actual area of a through hole, and S0 represents the area of a circle having a diameter equal to the long axis of that through hole. This shape ratio indicates the degree to which the through-hole shape approaches a circular or compact form. By ensuring that at least half of the through holes fall within this shape-ratio range, the aluminum plate can achieve improved uniformity in hole geometry, contributing to favorable coating behavior and reliable adhesion of active materials while maintaining strength.
outputs.L4:
An aluminum plate and a method for manufacturing the aluminum plate are provided. The aluminum plate is designed to exhibit excellent adhesion to an active material and improved coating characteristics while maintaining sufficient mechanical strength. These properties are achieved by forming a plurality of through holes in the aluminum plate and carefully controlling the geometry, size, distribution, and shape of the through holes.

The aluminum plate includes a metal aluminum substrate having multiple through holes that penetrate from one surface of the plate to the opposite surface. By providing these through holes, the surface area of the plate is increased, and an active material applied to the plate can enter or engage with the holes. This improves mechanical anchoring between the aluminum plate and the active material layer, thereby enhancing adhesion and reducing the likelihood of peeling, cracking, or delamination during use. At the same time, the through holes are controlled so that the remaining aluminum framework retains enough strength to function as a stable support or current collector.

The through holes are formed within specified dimensional ranges. In particular, the average hole diameter is controlled so that the holes are large enough to receive coating material and improve adhesion, but not so large that the aluminum plate loses excessive strength. The opening ratio, which represents the proportion of the plate surface occupied by the through holes, is also maintained within a predetermined range. If the opening ratio is too low, the improvement in coating adhesion and active-material retention may be insufficient. If the opening ratio is too high, the rigidity, tensile strength, and handling properties of the aluminum plate may deteriorate. Therefore, an appropriate balance between open area and remaining metal area is established.

The aluminum plate is further characterized by a controlled size distribution of the through holes. By limiting variation in hole diameter, coating material can be applied more uniformly across the surface of the plate. A narrow or well-regulated distribution of hole sizes helps prevent uneven coating thickness, localized accumulation of active material, and regions of weak adhesion. This contributes to stable coating performance and improved reliability of the finished product.

In addition, the shape regularity of the through holes is controlled. The holes may be formed to have substantially circular, elliptical, polygonal, or otherwise regular shapes, while avoiding excessive deformation, tearing, burr formation, or irregular edges. Improved shape regularity allows active material to penetrate and adhere consistently and reduces stress concentration points that could otherwise lead to cracking or fracture of the aluminum plate. Smooth and uniform hole edges also improve the coating process and contribute to more consistent product quality.

A method for manufacturing the aluminum plate includes preparing an aluminum sheet or foil and forming a plurality of through holes under conditions selected to satisfy the desired ranges of hole diameter, opening ratio, size distribution, and shape regularity. The through holes may be produced by mechanical punching, etching, laser processing, chemical processing, electrochemical processing, or another suitable perforation technique. Manufacturing conditions such as processing energy, tool shape, etching time, feed rate, and spacing pattern are controlled so that the resulting perforated aluminum plate has the intended structure and performance.

After formation of the through holes, the aluminum plate may be subjected to additional treatments, such as cleaning, surface roughening, oxide-film adjustment, heat treatment, rolling, flattening, or removal of burrs and residues. These treatments may further improve coating compatibility, electrical conductivity, corrosion resistance, surface uniformity, and mechanical durability. An active material can then be applied to one or both surfaces of the aluminum plate by coating, filling, pressing, drying, or sintering, depending on the intended application.

Because the through-hole structure is optimized, the aluminum plate provides both high adhesion to coated active materials and high strength as a substrate. The plate is therefore suitable for applications requiring a lightweight, conductive, and mechanically reliable aluminum support with excellent coating properties. Examples include current collectors for batteries and capacitors, electrode substrates, catalyst supports, filter materials, heat-transfer components, and other products in which an aluminum plate must securely retain a functional coating while maintaining structural integrity.

An object is anything that can be identified as a distinct thing. It may be something physical, like a chair, a book, a stone, or a phone, or it may be something more abstract, like an idea, a goal, or a piece of data in a computer program. What makes an object recognizable is that it has certain qualities, such as shape, size, color, purpose, or function.

In everyday life, objects help us understand and organize the world around us. A cup is an object used for drinking, a key is an object used for opening locks, and a lamp is an object used to provide light. Each object has features that make it useful or meaningful.

In technology, the word “object” can also have a special meaning. In programming, an object is a structure that contains data and actions. For example, a digital “car” object might have information such as color, speed, and model, as well as actions like start, stop, or turn.

Overall, an object is something that can be named, described, and understood as a separate unit. Whether it exists in the physical world or in a digital system, an object plays an important role in how people think, communicate, and interact with their surroundings.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an aluminum plate with through holes used as an electrode current collector, including numerical ranges for hole diameter, opening ratio, hole size distribution, and shape factor S1/S0.
counterfactuals.output: An electrode current collector comprising an aluminum or aluminum-alloy plate having a plurality of through holes extending between opposing main surfaces thereof, wherein the through holes have an equivalent circular diameter of 0.05 mm to 3.0 mm, an opening ratio of 5% to 70% based on a projected area of the plate, and a hole size distribution in which at least 80% of the through holes have an equivalent circular diameter within ±30% of an average equivalent circular diameter. Each through hole has an opening shape satisfying a shape factor S1/S0 of 1.0 to 1.5, where S1 is an actual perimeter length or actual opening contour length of the through hole and S0 is a perimeter length of a perfect circle having the same projected opening area as the through hole. The aluminum plate provides improved retention of electrode active material, reduced electrical resistance, and enhanced ion permeability while maintaining mechanical strength suitable for use as a positive or negative electrode current collector in an electrochemical device.

The aluminum plate is characterized in that:

   The through-holes have an average opening diameter of **0.1 μm or more and 100 μm or less**.

2. **Opening ratio**

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the “object of the invention” and main claim summary for a perforated aluminum plate, where the through holes have an average opening diameter of 0.1–100 μm, an opening ratio of 2–40%, and defined distributions for holes ≤5 μm, ≥40 μm, and S1/S0 values.
counterfactuals.output:
## Object of the Invention

An object of the invention is to provide a perforated aluminum plate having a large number of fine through holes, which achieves a controlled balance between permeability, surface area, mechanical strength, and uniformity of hole formation.

More specifically, the invention aims to provide a perforated aluminum plate in which the through holes have a fine average opening diameter of 0.1 to 100 μm and an opening ratio of 2 to 40%, while suppressing excessive variation in hole size and hole shape. By controlling the distribution of very small holes having an opening diameter of 5 μm or less, large holes having an opening diameter of 40 μm or more, and the ratio S1/S0 relating to hole-shape uniformity, the plate can exhibit stable filtration, diffusion, electrochemical, acoustic, heat-transfer, or bonding characteristics while maintaining sufficient strength as an aluminum substrate.

The invention further seeks to provide a perforated aluminum plate suitable for applications requiring fine and uniform permeability, such as current collectors, electrodes, filters, separators, catalyst supports, heat-dissipation members, sound-absorbing members, or functional metal substrates.

---

## Main Claim Summary

The invention relates to a perforated aluminum plate comprising an aluminum plate body having a plurality of through holes extending through the plate in a thickness direction.

The through holes are characterized in that:

1. **Average opening diameter**  
   The through holes have an average opening diameter of **0.1 to 100 μm**.

2. **Opening ratio**  
   The plate has an opening ratio, defined as the total area of openings relative to the surface area of the aluminum plate, of **2 to 40%**.

3. **Distribution of small holes**  
   A proportion of through holes having an opening diameter of **5 μm or less** is controlled within a predetermined range, for example so that excessively small holes do not dominate the hole population.

4. **Distribution of large holes**  
   A proportion of through holes having an opening diameter of **40 μm or more** is controlled within a predetermined range, thereby suppressing the presence of oversized holes that may reduce strength or impair uniformity.

5. **Hole-shape uniformity / S1/S0 value**  
   The through holes satisfy a defined range of **S1/S0**, where S0 represents a reference opening area or projected opening area of a hole and S1 represents a measured or corrected opening area associated with the hole geometry. By controlling the S1/S0 value, the invention ensures that the through holes have a desired degree of shape regularity, penetration quality, or opening uniformity.

In one representative claim format, the main claim may be expressed as follows:

> A perforated aluminum plate comprising an aluminum plate having a plurality of through holes,  
> wherein the through holes have an average opening diameter of 0.1 to 100 μm,  
> wherein an opening ratio of the through holes is 2 to 40%,  
> wherein a proportion of through holes having an opening diameter of 5 μm or less is within a predetermined first range,  
> wherein a proportion of through holes having an opening diameter of 40 μm or more is within a predetermined second range, and  
> wherein the through holes satisfy a predetermined S1/S0 range.

If desired, the claim can be further narrowed by specifying the actual numerical limits for:

- percentage of holes having an opening diameter ≤5 μm;
- percentage of holes having an opening diameter ≥40 μm; and
- allowable S1/S0 range.

counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A method for manufacturing an aluminum plate having excellent adhesion to active materials, high mechanical strength, and a plurality of through holes with controlled diameter and shape parameters is provided. The method includes preparing an aluminum or aluminum alloy plate, subjecting at least one surface of the plate to a roughening treatment to form an uneven surface suitable for anchoring an active material layer, and forming a plurality of through holes in the plate by controlled perforation processing. The through holes are formed so that at least one of an average opening diameter, a taper angle, a hole density, an aperture ratio, and a circularity or shape factor falls within a predetermined range. The perforation processing may include chemical etching, electrochemical etching, laser processing, mechanical punching, or a combination thereof, followed by a correction or finishing treatment for adjusting the hole profile. The aluminum plate may further be subjected to heat treatment, rolling, or surface modification to improve tensile strength and suppress deformation during subsequent coating and pressing steps. By controlling both the surface roughness and the geometry of the through holes, the obtained aluminum plate exhibits improved adhesion to electrode active materials, maintains sufficient strength, and enables stable penetration of slurry or electrolyte through the holes. The aluminum plate is particularly suitable for use as a current collector or support member in electrochemical devices such as lithium-ion batteries, capacitors, and other energy storage devices.
